name: agent-desktop
works_with: Any coding agent through the CLI, MCP or a skill; macOS, Windows and Linux
short: A computer use CLI that lets your AI agent read and operate desktop apps through the accessibility tree, with no screenshots.
what: agent-desktop reads a desktop app's accessibility tree and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check, and repeats. It has no model inside; the loop lives in your agent. It ships as a CLI, an MCP server and a C library.
who: Developers who want an agent to drive native desktop apps on macOS, Windows or Linux. You need your own agent to run the loop.
needs: Node.js with npm (or Bun, Yarn, pnpm), or Homebrew on macOS and Linux
macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 1809 or later, or Ubuntu 24.04 or later

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: On macOS and Linux, `brew install agent-desktop` also works.

steps.title: Check your setup
steps.text: On macOS the second command walks you through the Accessibility grant.

steps.title: Or add it as an MCP server
steps.text: Every command becomes an MCP tool, such as `desktop_snapshot` and `desktop_click`.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i` to list Finder's interactive elements with refs, click one with `agent-desktop click` and its ref, then snapshot again to check.

watch: It needs accessibility access, which lets it read and operate every app on your desktop.
Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots and debug files can contain private desktop content. The README says to keep them out of public logs and uploads.
Actions are headless by default, with no pointer movement or focus change. `--headed` uses real input.
In PowerShell, quote every ref, because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator.
